decision_reason: A1 leaves the low-U_NN pair standing still versus sitting and relaxing separated only by global posture inclination, while the highest-D_kNN class jump front & back lacks explicit contrasts for gravity-axis motion and repeated translation reversal. The broad rotational_motion attribute also conflates arm-dominant and ankle-dominant movement despite separately instrumented lower-arm and ankle segments. A2 therefore adds multisegment flexion, vertical translation, and translation-direction persistence, splits rotational motion by instrumented segment, and drops motion_regularity because all supplied A1 class prototypes assign it the same level.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: arm_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the instrumented right lower-arm segment during the activity.

levels.Low: Little or no lower-arm angular motion.

attributes.name: ankle_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the segment observed at the instrumented left ankle during the activity.

levels.Low: Little or no ankle-segment angular motion.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: multisegment_flexion
attributes.definition: Degree of sustained flexion in the body configuration indicated by gravity-relative orientation differences among the instrumented chest, lower-arm, and ankle segments.

levels.Low: Predominantly extended or mutually aligned segment configuration.

attributes.name: vertical_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of translational motion along the gravity-relative vertical direction, distinct from static body inclination.

levels.Low: Little or no vertical translational motion.
levels.Medium: Moderate or repeated vertical translational motion.
levels.High: Prominent large-amplitude, elevation-changing, or ballistic vertical motion.

attributes.name: translation_direction_persistence
attributes.definition: Degree to which translational motion maintains a consistent progression direction over time rather than stopping or repeatedly reversing.

levels.Low: No sustained progression or frequent translation-direction reversals.
levels.Medium: Partly sustained progression with occasional reversals or interruptions.
levels.High: Sustained translation predominantly in a consistent progression direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a transferable distinction between static postures and vigorous unseen activities, with jogging and climbing stairs providing seen high-intensity anchors.
Repetition rate provides an independent distinction between faster running cycles and the slower or absent repetition of static postures, while cycling supplies a seen high-cadence anchor.
Sustained rapid fluctuation is physically distinct from energy and isolated impacts and helps contrast running and jump front & back with smooth static postures and cycling.
Short high-magnitude impacts are a clear transferable property of running and jumping that is not captured by average intensity or sustained roughness.
Mean gravity-relative global inclination preserves the primary upright-to-horizontal posture continuum linking standing still and sitting and relaxing to the seen lying down prototype.
Time-varying global posture distinguishes repeated whole-body displacement in jump front & back from stable postures and complements mean inclination.

The broad A1 concept assigns the same prominence to physically different arm-dominant, ankle-dominant, and whole-body actions. Separate gyroscope-equipped lower-arm and ankle scopes preserve angular motion while adding a transferable contrast between frontal elevation of arms, knees bending (crouching), locomotion, and jumping.
Overall sustained progression remains necessary for relating running to seen locomotion and for contrasting it with the bounded front-and-back translation of jumping.

All supplied A1 class prototypes assign motion_regularity the same High level, so it provides no split-specific semantic contrast. Cadence retains repetition rate, while smoothness and impulsiveness retain complementary temporal-structure information.

Standing still and sitting and relaxing have very low unseen-pair separation in A1 and differ mainly by inclination. Static orientation relations across the chest, lower arm, and ankle provide an independent extended-versus-flexed configuration contrast, with knees bending (crouching) as a seen flexion anchor and lying down as an inclined but comparatively extended anchor.

The weakly covered jump front & back class includes pronounced gravity-axis displacement that overall translation does not isolate. Climbing stairs and knees bending (crouching) provide seen support for vertical body motion, while jogging supports a lower-amplitude locomotor comparison.

Running normally sustains progression whereas jump front & back repeatedly reverses its translation direction. This contrast is independent of translation magnitude and transfers from the directionally persistent seen locomotion classes walking, jogging, climbing stairs, and cycling.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes separate complementary physical questions. Motion_intensity measures overall energy, smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation, and impulsiveness measures isolated peaks. Cadence measures repetition rate and does not duplicate any retained regularity attribute. Posture_inclination measures mean global orientation, posture_variability measures its temporal change, and multisegment_flexion measures static or sustained configuration across body segments; thus sitting, standing, and lying need not be represented by one inclination coordinate alone. Arm_rotational_motion and ankle_rotational_motion are nonoverlapping segment scopes rather than duplicate global rotation measures. Translational_motion measures overall sustained progression, vertical_translation isolates its gravity-axis component, and translation_direction_persistence measures whether progression maintains or reverses direction. Each concept is ordinal and is supportable in principle by the available accelerometer, gyroscope, gravity-orientation, periodicity, jerk, translation-proxy, and multiaxial coupling capabilities.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
